thread:
maria: Heads up — customer on prod seeing SSE chat streams drop after ~25–35s behind ALB + Cloudflare. They get a partial message then the client reconnects and sometimes sees duplicate tokens billed. Repro steps below.

maria: Repro (condensed):
1) curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat\" -d \"{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}\"
2) let idle for 30s, server sends heartbeat chunk like: `:\n` or `event: keepalive\n\n`
3) after ~30s connection is reset; client sees truncated chunk and reconnects.

maria: Server logs show:
```
[2025-10-12T15:04:12Z] connection established, id=abcd
[2025-10-12T15:04:36Z] wrote 128 bytes (heartbeat)
[2025-10-12T15:04:37Z] recv RST_STREAM / half-close from upstream
[2025-10-12T15:04:37Z] downstream connection reset by peer
```

tariq: Maybe ALB idle timeout or Cloudflare buffering kicking in. Can you confirm ALB target-group idle timeout and whether Cloudflare is in front with proxy buffering enabled?

maria: Customer uses ALB (default idle timeout 60s) + Cloudflare in front with \"Always Online\" off but \"Response Buffering\" default (they didn't customize). ALB target logs show target connection closed right after the heartbeat.

leo: Two likely interactions: 1) ALB or nginx may be half-closing while Cloudflare still expects streaming => truncated chunk. 2) If any proxy is buffering whole responses (or doing gzip aggregation) it can swallow tiny heartbeat chunks.

leo: Quick workarounds to try (low-risk):
- ensure server sends non-empty heartbeat payload every 15s (e.g. `data: \"\\n\"\n\n`) not just a comment line — some proxies drop `:`-style comments.
- set ALB idle timeout > 120s (we recommend 180s for long-lived streams)
- on origin/proxy set `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` explicitly and disable response buffering (nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection '';`)
- for Cloudflare, try enabling \"Origin Keepalive\" and disable response buffering/response body minification, or use a bypass Page Rule for the endpoint

cloudflare-sre: Note — Cloudflare tiers differ. In our experience the free/cheap plans may coalesce tiny chunks; the Enterprise level supports true streaming with micro-chunks preserved. If you can't change plan, try larger heartbeat chunks (~512 bytes) to avoid coalescing. Also check Cloudflare's \"HTTP/2 to Origin\" behavior which can change timing.

maria: Tried 1) changed heartbeat to 512 bytes every 20s and 2) ALB idle timeout -> 180s in a staging ALB. Staging shows much fewer truncations but still occasional half-close when Cloudflare goes through.

tariq: Could be ALB health/target drain race if connections hit a different target mid-stream. Verify target stickiness and connection reuse. Also check for intermediate WAF rules timing out lambda@edge or Cloudflare Workers.

maria: Customer also reported 502s on reconnects occasionally — suspect Cloudflare returns 502 when origin half-closed mid-chunk. We asked them to capture HAR from browser and we got partial payloads.

leo: Action items:
- support: escalate to infra to request ALB connection logging for the relevant time window (we need full tcp traces if possible).
- engineering: add an optional server-side tiny-body-on-heartbeat flag that emits 256–512 bytes to keep proxies honest.
- support: provide customer a test URL that bypasses Cloudflare (host header + /nocache path) to confirm origin-only behavior.

supportbot: Created ticket INF-2321 and linked customer case #C-9987.

ingest-bot: automated note: alerting spike matched 2025-10-12T15:04–15:06 window, ~14% reconnect rate for that customer.

maria: Thanks — I'll run through suggested workarounds with the customer and ask infra for ALB tcp logs. If we confirm Cloudflare behavior is the proximate cause we'll ask them to try bypass/test URL. Will update here. :thumbsup:
